A hard low shaft from behind the mass turns every crown of white down into a ring of fire against deep emerald shade, and the coarse weave of one sack thrown over a stem glows amber where the edge of the beam clips it.

The whole canopy above is lit hot russet and gold, so the scene stands in warm reflected colour with teal shade underneath, and one wet stem inside the shade throws back a single hard copper highlight.

One narrow shaft strikes a rising column of silk so it lights straight through like smoke, rose-gold and grainy against cool indigo, while the ribbed stem beside it takes only a hard bright highlight along one edge.

Late almost-level sun from one side lays a long ember stripe down every ribbed stem it reaches and puts a hot gold rim on every papery blade spinning past, everything beyond that reach going deep indigo.

The sky beyond the stand has gone bright bone-white, so every stem, every seed sailing across it, and one shoulder read as warm ember-orange shapes against it, with one narrow band of cool teal holding the very bottom of the frame.

A low shaft from behind catches only the down snagged on bark, so the whole near surface burns with a hundred small bright points of white fire against plum shade, and each point carries its own small halo where the light bends round the fibres.

Light comes down through a sheet of russet leaf overhead, so the underside of the whole scene is lit copper, the mat of leaves underfoot doubling the warmth, with cool emerald shade climbing the far stems.
One burning patch of gold is thrown onto the mat of leaves underfoot, the rest of the scene in cool teal shade, and a woven sack sitting in the gold patch glows ochre right through to its seams.

The air has gone thick and amber-gold with the stuff racing through it, the light arriving grainy through the mass, and the far stems haze out rose while the near bark stays hard-edged and copper-lit.

Rain just stopped, and every wet stem throws back one hard bright highlight against saturated emerald green, the pooled water in a bark hollow going rose-gold where the sky beyond the stand has brightened to bone-white.
Light coming through a fae's own wing from behind turns it amber with its veins reading as dark lines through it, while everything surrounding that wing stays cool blue-grey and unlit.

A squall's cloud edge lets one sheet of copper light in low from behind the stand while everything above goes indigo, so the papery blades racing through it each catch fire along their trailing edges.

A hard shaft from directly behind the mass pours through the whole column of white tufts at once, turning them rose-gold and grainy against blue-grey, and one hooked seed-ball stuck in bark at the edge blazes amber.
The canopy overhead is lit hot gold and the reflected warmth fills the scene from above, so the ribbed stems glow ochre on their upper faces and cool teal shade pools deep along their lower flanks.

One narrow shaft from behind strikes a single rising column of silk and lights it straight through, bone-white and blazing, while the hundred tufts streaming past on either side stay in cool emerald shadow completely.

Late sun from one side skims in under the canopy almost level, putting a copper rim on every papery blade cartwheeling through the air and a long gold streak along the mat of leaves below, indigo shade beyond.

A single sheet of copper light comes in low under a cloud edge and lights only the upper half of the stand, every tuft crossing it going briefly gold, while the near stems stay solid indigo and keep their own hard edges.
A low shaft from behind lights only the down caught on cloth, so a shoulder and the side of a jaw are outlined in white fire against plum shade, the ribbed stem at the border taking one gold edge.

Copper light comes down through a split in the canopy and lands as a hard bright patch on the coarse weave of a sack, the rest in cool teal shade, with one papery blade spinning through the patch going briefly amber.

A hard low shaft through a gap in the stems from behind strikes the streaming mass edge-on, every crown of down burning white against deep emerald, and the hollow of one stem at the border goes rose-gold inside.

One shaft from behind lights a column of silk straight through like smoke, amber and grainy, the far stems hazing rose in the thick air, while the near bark stays hard-edged and cool blue-grey entirely.

Late almost-level light from one side puts a hot gold rim on every spinning papery blade in the air and lays an ember stripe down the ribbed stem filling the near side, deep indigo shade on everything else.

The sky beyond the stand gone bright bone-white so every tuft racing across it and every stem behind the fae reads warm ochre against it, the mat of leaves underfoot catching one last pool of amber where the light gets through.

A squall's trailing edge lets copper light in from behind the whole stand, low and hard, while the sky above turns indigo, so a hundred tufts bolting through the gap each ignite as a brief ring of white fire.

Rain just stopped and the wet bark on the near stem throws back one brilliant gold highlight against saturated emerald, every wet vein on the leaves underfoot doing the same, the sky beyond gone bone-white and bright.
